name: Shared filtering core (Rust)
description:
The filtering engine. One implementation, used by both platforms, with no OS calls in it. Per Project Guidelines §3, all filtering logic lives here and nowhere else.

CURRENT STATE: nothing built. The Python prototypes in the session scratchpad (expand.py, generic.py) prove the expansion arithmetic works against real libphonenumber metadata across all 245 territories; they are throwaway and this feature replaces them.

API SHAPE:
  normalize(raw, defaultRegion) -> E164
  evaluate(E164, RuleSet) -> Allow | Block | Silence | Label(text)
  geocode(E164, language) -> Country / Region / City
  expand(Rule, limit) -> sorted exact numbers, or TooBroad(count)
  explain(Rule) -> expansion count + per-platform verdict

WHAT IT MUST DO:
- Rule model covering exact number, pattern, starts-with, ends-with, prefix, caller ID, and location, each as deny or allow (R2).
- Precedence: most specific wins, so an allow on an exact number beats a deny on the range containing it. Equally specific conflicts are reported, never silently resolved.
- Expansion for iOS calls, driven by possibleLengths AND nationalNumberPattern. The regex must prune — length-summing alone materially overestimates, badly for landlines (DE fixedLine has 11 possible lengths, 5 to 15).
- Allow-exceptions resolved at expansion time by set subtraction, since CallKit has no allow list.
- Prefix-to-place geocoding. The `phonenumber` crate (0.3.10+9.0.33) gives parse/validate/format but NO geocoder — we implement it as a prefix trie over libphonenumber's geocoding files, with user-language then English then prefix-only fallback (R7).
- Report expansion size and per-platform verdict for any rule, from real data (R2 honesty requirement).

CONSTRAINTS: no country, prefix, length or place name in code (Guidelines §1) — all of it comes from the datasets in F003. The entry limit is injected configuration measured in F001, never a constant (Guidelines §4). Rules are the stored truth; expansions are derived and never persisted as rules (Guidelines §2).

Exposed to Kotlin and Swift via UniFFI. Rust was chosen over Kotlin Multiplatform because its C ABI also reaches HarmonyOS if Huawei is ever taken on.

TESTABILITY: this feature is pure logic with no platform dependency, so it can be fully tested on the host before either app exists. It should be, since a filtering bug here is a bug on every platform at once.
